extracted.intended_audience: registrants' SEC reporting teams, corporate accountants and legal counsel preparing registration statements and proxy materials for acquisitions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on which financial statements of an acquired business must be included or updated in SEC registration statements and proxy materials (Rule 3-05 / S-X rules), including timing/age, availability, relief conditions, and filer-status differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include Rule 3-05 financial statements when acquiree not included for full fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 3-05 financial statements for an acquired business must be included in a registration statement when a complete fiscal year of the acquired business’s operating results has not been included in the registrant’s audited financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: If an acquisition is significant (>40%) and the acquiree was included in consolidated statements for less than one year, include audited annual financial statements for specified prior years and unaudited interim statements updated to a later quarter (e.g., audited as of and for years ended Dec 31, 20X2 and 20X1; unaudited interim as of Sept 30, 20X3 and for nine months ended Sept 30, 20X3 and 20X2). See Rule 3-05 periods required examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted financial statements when effective/mailing date falls within 45 days after acquiree year-end
rubrics_metrics.description: If the anticipated effective date of a registration statement or the proposed mailing date of proxy material falls within 45 days after the acquired business’s fiscal year-end, registrant may provide preceding fiscal year audited statements (not the most recent) and unaudited interim statements for the third quarter of the most recently completed fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if audited financial statements for the most recently completed fiscal year are available, those must be included. (S-X Rule 3-12(b), S-X Rule 8-08). Registrants must update the filing with audited statements if they become available before the effective date or mailing date. See interpretive response to Question 4.4.100.

rubrics_metrics.name: When financial statements are considered 'available'
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements are considered available no later than when they are issued: either (a) widely distributed to all shareholders and other users in a GAAP-compliant format (and for annual financials, with an audit report indicating auditors complied with GAAS/PCAOB standards), or (b) filed with the SEC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting on a registrant's website counts as wide distribution if the website is used for public disclosure. For nonpublic entities, statements are 'available' if they are available to be issued (i.e., complete and approved by required parties). Completion of the audit and necessary approvals (management, board, audit committee) make statements available to be issued. (Topic 855; FRM references).

rubrics_metrics.name: S-X Rule 3-01(c) relief conditions (registrant must satisfy)
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for relief from including the most recently completed fiscal year financial statements of an acquired business when the effective/mailing date is later than 45 days but still close to the acquiree year-end, the registrant (not the acquiree) must meet specified conditions in S-X Rule 3-01(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conditions: (1) registrant files reports under Exchange Act sections 13 or 15(d) and is current on filings; (2) registrant reasonably and in good faith expects to report income attributable to the registrant, after taxes, for the most recently completed fiscal year prior to the acquisition date; (3) registrant reported income attributable to the registrant for at least one of the two fiscal years immediately preceding the most recent fiscal year. (S-X Rule 3-01(c), Rule 8-08(b)). Note: Condition 2 is applied based on registrant’s most recently completed fiscal year prior to the acquisition even if audited statements exist for that year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filer-status specific relief timing (days after acquiree year-end)
rubrics_metrics.description: When Rule 3-01(c) relief applies, the third-quarter interim financial statements of the acquired business's previous year are considered the most recent required statements if the effective/mailing date falls before filer-status-specific cutoff days after the acquiree's year-end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cutoffs: large accelerated filer — 60 days; accelerated filer — 75 days; non-accelerated filer (including nonpublic entity) — 90 days. For SRCs meeting S-X Rule 8-08(b), third-quarter interim statements are timely if before the 90th day. (S-X Rule 3-12(b), 3-12(g)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include audited financial statements if effective/mailing date is after relief dates
rubrics_metrics.description: If the effective date or mailing date is after the filer-status specific days indicated (or after the 45-day-to-relief-window and the registrant does not satisfy Rule 3-01(c) or Rule 8-08(b)), audited financial statements of the acquired business for the most recent fiscal year must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See S-X Rule 3-01(d) and FRM 2045.5. Examples show when relief is unavailable (e.g., effective date beyond 89 days for some scenarios) and an amendment will be required to update to the most recent audited year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of accounting acquirer’s reporting history in reverse acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: In a reverse acquisition, the historical financial statements and reporting history of the accounting acquirer (considered the 'registrant') are used to assess the registrant’s ability to meet S-X Rule 3-01(c) (or Rule 8-08(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This determines whether financial statements of the accounting acquirer must be updated. (FRM 12220.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining required age/periods of Rule 3-05 financials when registrant and acquiree year-ends differ
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate S-X Rule 3-01(c) conditions using the registrant’s most recently completed fiscal year (and two preceding years) to determine required age/periods of Rule 3-05 financial statements; acquiree's statements are not relevant to the evaluation of those conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stepwise approach: (1) determine information used to evaluate conditions; (2) determine required age based on whether conditions met. Examples illustrate differing required periods for acquiree vs registrant depending on whether conditions #2 and #3 are met (income vs loss scenarios).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief/exception availability when Rule 3-05 would require acquiree financials more recent than registrant’s
rubrics_metrics.description: If Rule 3-12 or Rule 8-08 would require audited financial statements of the acquiree that are more recent than those required for the registrant, limited relief may be requested if providing more recent audited financials imposes an unreasonable burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant may request relief from the Office of the Chief Accountant prior to filing and should be prepared to provide the acquiree's financial statements updated on an unaudited basis through either the registrant's latest balance sheet date or the acquiree's year-end. See chapter 10 for requesting relief. (FRM 2045.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: When Rule 3-01(c) relief is unavailable based on timing thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 3-01(c) relief is not available if a registration statement becomes effective or proxy material is mailed more than certain days after the acquiree’s fiscal year-end (different thresholds depending on filer status).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relief is not available if effective/mailing date is more than 89 days (or 74/59 days if acquiree is accelerated or large accelerated filer, respectively) after the fiscal year-end. In such cases, audited financial statements for the most recent fiscal year of the acquiree must be included. (S-X Rule 3-01(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include unaudited interim financial statements when effective date beyond 134 days after acquiree year-end
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registration statement’s effective date is 135 or more days (130 days if acquiree is an accelerated filer or large accelerated filer) after the acquiree’s year-end, the filing must include unaudited interim financial statements as of a date and for a period ending fewer than those day thresholds before the expected effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, proxy statements mailed more than 134 days (129 days for accelerated/large accelerated) after the acquiree’s year-end must include such unaudited interim statements. (S-X Rule 3-12(a), Rule 8-08).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to seek accelerated effective date to avoid additional update burden
rubrics_metrics.description: SEC staff may accelerate the effective date of a registrant’s registration statement (thereby avoiding later required updates) if certain conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions for acceleration include: registrant timely filed all Exchange Act reports in last 12 months; interim financial statements in the filing are at least as recent as the quarterly information required by the Exchange Act at time of effectiveness. SEC may request confirmation that the next quarterly report will be timely filed and that no material trends/events arose after the latest balance sheet date that materially affect investor understanding. (FRM 1220.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-known seasoned issuers (WKSIs) are not exempt from age requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A WKSI is not exempt from the age of financial statement requirements with respect to itself and all completed and probable acquirees at the time a shelf registration statement becomes effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although a WKSI’s shelf registration may become effective upon filing, it still must comply with the age requirements. WKSI definition and eligibility criteria (Form S-3/F-3 thresholds, public float or prior securities issuance) are noted. (FRM 2045.4; Reg C Rule 405).

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to update pre-acquisition interim statements beyond most recent completed quarter if omitted period is less than a quarter
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-acquisition interim period financial statements of the acquired business are not required beyond the most recently completed quarter before the acquisition if the omitted period is less than a complete quarter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, disclosure of significant events occurring during the omitted interim period may be necessary. A registrant must file financial statements audited through the date of acquisition for any business deemed a predecessor. (FRM 2045.9). Example provided showing when no interim statements are required because balance sheet date of annual statements is fewer than 135 days from effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: If cutoff last day is non-working day, filing may be made next business day without updating
rubrics_metrics.description: If the last day of the period after which financial statements must be updated (e.g., the 134th day after a quarter-end) falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or holiday, the filing may be made on the next business day without updating the financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: FRM 1220.12; Reg C Rule 417. See discussion of updating requirements at Question 4.4.40.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum age of Rule 3-05 financial statements for an IPO registration statement
rubrics_metrics.description: For an IPO registration statement, the most recent audited financial statements required by Rule 3-05 must not be more than one year and 45 days old at the date the registration statement becomes effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S-X Rule 3-12(d) sets this requirement. Note S-X Rule 8-08 has no similar requirement; SRCs have differing filing up-to timing if they meet conditions in Rule 8-08(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional disclosures required for multiple acquisitions that individually do not require audited financials
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple acquisitions individually are below thresholds (or temporarily not required under 75-day grace), but their aggregate impact exceeds 50%, the registrant must provide additional disclosures and financial information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant must provide pro forma financial information under S-X Rules 11-01 and 11-02 depicting the aggregate impact in all material respects, and financial statements covering at least the most recent fiscal year and most recent interim period for any acquired business for which financial statements are not yet required solely because of the 75-day grace. The aggregate measurement is since the registrant’s latest audited fiscal year-end balance sheet; filing the Form 10-K gives a fresh start on aggregate measurement. (S-X Rule 3-05(b)(2)(iv), Question 4.4.230).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule that a registrant must update filings if audited financial statements become available before effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: If audited financial statements for a period were not included because they were not available at filing, the registrant must update the filing with those audited financial statements if they become available before the registration statement's effective date or the proxy mailing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated in the interpretive response to availability and updating (FRM 1220.3). Example guidance indicates amended filings may be required to include newly available audited annual financials.
